title: Pinning AeST's Free Background Parameter: Q0 = 3e-3 - 1.5e-2 Mpc^-1 from Galaxy-Scale Phenomenology
description: The Aether-Scalar-Tensor theory (AeST; Skordis and Zlosnik 2021, PRL 127 161302) reproduces the Planck CMB power spectrum and the galaxy-scale radial acceleration relation, but leaves the scalar background rate Q0 = phi-bar-dot free -- its authors state explicitly that the dark-sector density is 'not (classically) predicted', and their three published fits span four orders of magnitude in Q0 (1e-4, 1e-1, 1 Mpc^-1). We show that a framework built on AeST with three additional commitments -- the dark-sector shift charge carrying the FULL dark-matter abundance (rho = Q0 n), the selection beta = 1, and w = -1 exactly -- collapses that freedom to a ONE-PARAMETER FAMILY, because the resulting relation Q0 = sqrt(Lambda) R_dm/(nu0 mu) is one equation in two unknowns. Galaxy-scale phenomenology then fixes the remaining coordinate: the framework's own kinematic identity slaves the condensate flow speed to the scalar gradient, and the same gradient must supply the static MOND force at radial-acceleration-relation radii. The result is Q0 = 3.4e-3 to 1.5e-2 Mpc^-1, equivalently K''(Q0) = 1e2 to 1e3, a region strictly interior to AeST's published fits. As an independent corroboration using no CMB information, expressing the result in the natural variable mu = sqrt(K''(Q0)) places BOTH of AeST's MOND-compatible published parameter sets inside the pinned band (mu = 122 and 195, band 33-1295) while the Higgs-type fit -- which Skordis and Zlosnik themselves call 'incompatible with a MOND limit' -- falls outside (mu = 41231). We are explicit about the limits: the pin is an order-of-magnitude CLASS statement rather than an equality (the two profiles equated have different radial shapes and the implied Q0 drifts by a factor 2.1-2.7 across 3.7-60 kpc); the value carries a CANDIDATE grade resting on one adversarially-refereed lane, though the identification of the framework's Q0 with AeST's own is derivation-grade and verified on five legs (units, cosmic time coordinate, background normalisation, kinetic normalisation, and the quasi-static relation) against the published source; K2 is pinned only to about three decades because the nu0 window propagates quadratically; lambda_s remains free; and kappa = 1/2 remains MEASURED (0.551 +/- 0.043), not derived. Most importantly, the result does NOT price the theory's nonlinear sector at recombination and cannot: AeST's authors note that a0 'does not appear in the linear cosmological regime but will play a role once nonlinear terms from F(Y,Q) kick in', which is precisely the regime at issue, so a Boltzmann computation carrying both the aether sector and the nonlinear branch at this framework's own kinetic function remains owed and is stated here as the sharpest open liability. The claim is narrow and checkable: IF one commits to the shift charge carrying the full dark-matter abundance with w = -1 exact, THEN galaxy-scale phenomenology alone selects a Q0 region interior to the published CMB fits, and specifically the region occupied by the MOND-compatible ones -- falsifiable by any CMB fit demanding Q0 outside 1e-3 to 1e-1 Mpc^-1. All quantitative claims are reproduced by committed scripts at https://github.com/carlzimmerman/zimmerman-formula, including the adversarial lane's own trial script and the standing retraction record.
notes: Short note. Publish as a NEW record. The contribution is the acceleration-scale normalisation and the three commitments that collapse AeST's Q0 freedom -- NOT the underlying theory, which is Skordis and Zlosnik's. Interpolation kernel: Milgrom and Sanders 2008, ApJ 678 131, Eq. (13) at alpha = 1/2. Strict both-ways discipline: the pin is CANDIDATE-graded, the recombination-side liability is stated rather than minimised, and an earlier version of that analysis was withdrawn (an error in the framework's own DISFAVOUR) and is recorded in RETRACTIONS.md. Reproducible from nbody_2026/stage56, stage57, stage58 and stage58_ev at https://github.com/carlzimmerman/zimmerman-formula.
